carbon_policy_signal.item: EU Parliament pushes tighter fossil fuel exclusions under SFDR (Sustainable Finance Directive); stricter capital restrictions on gas/coal plants raise cost of thermal generation.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Higher cost-of-capital for fossil fuel generation reduces supply willingness and lifts power prices and EUA demand as coal/gas plants retire or defer capex; structural carbon-bullish over months horizon.

freshness_caveat: Coal data stale as of 2025-12-26 (252 days old); Clean Dark and Clean Spark dated to year-end 2025 (247 days). Current thermal merit order and fuel-switch valuation cannot be reliably assessed without fresh derived spreads and coal pricing from September 2026.
risk_flags: Coal data is 252 days stale (as of 2025-12-26); daily headline may not reflect September 2026 supply fundamentals.
Clean Dark and Clean Spark both dated to year-end 2025; cannot reliably assess current thermal merit order without fresh derived spreads.
Slovakia sanctions holdout (news from Politico) could trigger rapid TTF re-rating upward if EU embargo weakens; no dated vote in brief.
Nuclear thermal stress (rising ambient temps) structural risk; competing with data-center demand surge for EU generation headroom.

base.summary: GB premium persists on local supply tightness; storage deficit supports TTF; coal stays undervalued pending fresh data.

downside.summary: EU sanctions hardened; summer heatwave stress on nuclear cooling reduces baseload capacity; data-center demand accelerates; GB premium widens continent-wide.

upside.summary: Slovakia sanctions vote blocks EU embargo renewal; Russian gas re-enters EU market, flooding TTF and suppressing power prices sharply.

themes: GB Power extreme tightness vs EU storage deficit
Sanctions erosion risk on Russian gas flows
Nuclear capacity threatened by thermal stress; data-center demand offsetting
Coal deeply undervalued; fuel-switch margin widening
top_drivers: GB Power at 98th percentile (177.71 EUR/MWh, +26.46% daily) driving GB-DE spread premium and thermal support.
EU storage deficit of 16.7 pp below seasonal (65.85% full) underpins winter supply risk and Cal+1 gas/power curve support.
Slovakia sanctions holdout on EU Russia embargo creates tail risk of cheap Russian gas inflow, weighing on TTF upside but creating asymmetry.
Nuclear cooling constraints from rising temperatures (climate stress) threaten baseload supply and force reliance on peaking thermal; structural bullish for power.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 98th percentile, EU storage 16.7 pp deficit, and Slovakia sanctions threat combine to support thermal; coal's 7th-percentile valuation signals fuel-switch headroom despite stale data.

watchlist.why: EU Russia energy embargo erosion would unleash TTF upside and suppress power prices; currently unpriced tail risk.

watchlist.metric: EU storage refill pace vs. seasonal deficit
watchlist.why: At 65.85% and 16.7 pp below seasonal, shortfall will constrain winter gas availability and support Cal+1 curve; watch withdrawal profile.

watchlist.metric: GB Power 98th percentile sustained or mean-revert
watchlist.why: At 177.71 EUR/MWh, GB is severely extended; supply shock or demand softening could re-rate sharply; transmission risk into continent.
Tighter capital restrictions on gas/coal plants will raise generation cost-of-capital and structurally support power/EUA; months horizon but directional.

watchlist.metric: US LNG +23% YoY (17.4 Bcf/d) arbitrage window to EU
watchlist.why: Higher volumes could compress TTF via improved LNG arb; currently supporting bearish-power narrative if cost-of-delivery to Europe tightens.
